Can you describe the color of the fluid draining from the ulcer if any, and has the surrounding redness extended rapidly in the last few days? REQUEST IMAGES: Right leg clinical photos.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of a painful ulcer with a central necrotic base, purplish irregular borders, pitting edema, and dilated tortuous veins following an ant bite is highly suggestive of cutaneous leishmaniasis or a severe deep fungal infection like sporotrichosis; however, given your diabetes and history of steroid use, we must rule out atypical bacterial cellulitis or pyoderma gangrenosum. Can you confirm if you have been traveling recently to tropical or subtropical regions? REQUEST TEST: Tissue biopsy for histopathology and culture. REQUEST IMAGES: Right leg clinical photos.

text: RESULTS: Histopathology: Neutrophilic infiltration without infection, consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum. The histopathology showing neutrophilic infiltration without evidence of infection, combined with your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and the characteristic appearance of the ulcer with purplish borders, confirms this diagnosis.
